content: The text provided is a list of references from various studies, articles, and clinical trials related to the diagnosis, treatment, and management of cryptococcal meningitis, particularly in the context of HIV-infected individuals. 1. There is an urgent need to address the global accessibility of a 50-year-old antifungal medication, as highlighted in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2013. 2. Lightowler JV and colleagues conducted a study on the treatment of cryptococcal meningitis in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, published in PLoS One in 2010. 3. Kambugu A and collaborators examined the outcomes of cryptococcal meningitis in Uganda before and after the introduction of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART), as reported in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2008. 4. Bicanic T et al. explored the relationship between cerebrospinal fluid pressure, fungal burden, and patient outcomes in cryptococcal meningitis cases undergoing serial lumbar punctures, published in AIDS in 2009. 5. Graybill JR and colleagues provided guidelines for the diagnosis and management of increased intracranial pressure in AIDS patients with cryptococcal meningitis, as part of the NIAID Mycoses Study Group and AIDS Cooperative Treatment Groups, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2000. 6. The World Health Organization issued rapid advice on the diagnosis, prevention, and management of cryptococcal disease in HIV-infected adults, adolescents, and children, accessible online as of January 2018. 7. Rolfes MA and collaborators investigated the impact of therapeutic lumbar punctures on acute mortality in cryptococcal meningitis, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2014. 8. Likasitwattanakul S et al. studied cryptococcosis in HIV-infected children in Southeast Asia, with findings published in the Southeast Asian Journal of Tropical Medicine and Public Health in 2004. 9. Abadi J and colleagues reported on cryptococcosis in children with AIDS, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1999. 10. Mfinanga S and collaborators conducted a randomized controlled trial on cryptococcal meningitis screening and community-based early adherence support in advanced HIV patients starting antiretroviral therapy in Tanzania and Zambia, published in The Lancet in 2015. 11. Ford N et al. reviewed CD4 cell count thresholds for cryptococcal antigen screening in HIV-infected individuals, with findings in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 12. Jarvis JN and colleagues evaluated the cost-effectiveness of cryptococcal antigen screening to prevent HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis in South Africa, as published in PLoS One in 2013. 13. Cassim N et al. established the cost-per-result of laboratory-based reflex cryptococcal antigenemia screening in HIV-positive patients with CD4 counts below 100 cells/µL in South Africa, published in PLoS One in 2017. 14. Chipungu C and collaborators assessed the feasibility and acceptability of cryptococcal antigen screening in resource-limited HIV/AIDS clinics in Malawi, as reported in the Journal of the International Association of Providers of AIDS Care in 2015. 15. Meya DB et al. analyzed the cost-effectiveness of serum cryptococcal antigen screening to prevent deaths among HIV-infected individuals with CD4+ cell counts ≤100 cells/µL in resource-limited settings, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2010. 16. Rajasingham R and colleagues proposed integrating cryptococcal antigen screening and preemptive treatment into routine HIV care, as published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012. 17. Smith RM et al. studied the prevalence of cryptococcal antigenemia and the cost-effectiveness of a cryptococcal antigen screening program in Vietnam, published in PLoS One in 2013. 18. Vidal JE and collaborators reported on asymptomatic cryptococcal antigen prevalence detected by lateral flow assay in hospitalized HIV-infected patients in São Paulo, Brazil, published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2016. 19. Awotiwon A et al. reviewed strategies for preventing cryptococcal infection in people living with HIV, as part of the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 20. Hakim J and colleagues evaluated enhanced prophylaxis combined with antiretroviral therapy for advanced HIV infection in Africa, as published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2017. 21. Parkes-Ratanshi R et al. conducted a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial on primary prophylaxis of cryptococcal disease with fluconazole in HIV-positive Ugandan adults, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2011. 22. Ford N et al. systematically reviewed causes of hospital admission among people living with HIV worldwide, published in The Lancet HIV in 2015. 23. Larson BA and collaborators assessed the cost-effectiveness of alternative screening strategies for cryptococcal antigenemia in HIV-infected patients with low CD4 counts in South Africa, published in PLoS One in 2016. 24. Vallabhaneni S et al. evaluated a public-sector, provider-initiated cryptococcal antigen screening and treatment program in the Western Cape, South Africa, published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016. 25. Rick F and colleagues conducted a feasibility study on cryptococcal antigen screening using a rapid test at the point of care in rural Lesotho, published in PLoS One in 2017. 26. Wake RM et al. demonstrated that high cryptococcal antigen titers in blood predict subclinical cryptococcal meningitis among HIV-infected patients, as reported in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 27. Molloy S and collaborators studied antifungal combinations for treating cryptococcal meningitis in Africa, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2018. 28. Brouwer MC et al. reviewed the use of corticosteroids for acute bacterial meningitis, as part of the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2015. 29. Beardsley J et al. investigated the role of adjunctive dexamethasone in HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2016. 30. Bahr NC et al. demonstrated that standardized electrolyte supplementation and fluid management improve survival during amphotericin therapy for cryptococcal meningitis in resource-limited settings, published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases in 2014. 31. Echevarria J et al. evaluated the use of oral rehydration solutions to prevent nephrotoxicity associated with amphotericin B, published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2006. 32. Girmenia C and collaborators studied the effects of hydration with salt repletion on renal toxicity during conventional amphotericin B therapy, published in Supportive Care in Cancer in 2005. 33. Thakur CP et al. improved treatment outcomes for kala-azar by supplementing amphotericin B with physiologic saline and potassium chloride, published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2010. 34. Park MK et al. reported on the treatment of hydrocephalus secondary to cryptococcal meningitis using shunting, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1999. 35. Sun HY et al. discussed the management of cryptococcal meningitis with extremely high intracranial pressure in HIV-infected patients, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2004. 36. Yuchong C et al. explored lumbar puncture drainage with intrathecal amphotericin B injection for controlling cryptococcal meningitis, published in Mycoses in 2011. 37. Meda J et al. evaluated the management of cryptococcal meningitis in Tanzania using a strict schedule of serial lumbar punctures, published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2014. 38. Shoham S et al. assessed healthcare providers' adherence to published practice guidelines for managing cryptococcal disease, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2005. 39. Newton PN et al. conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of acetazolamide for treating elevated intracranial pressure in cryptococcal meningitis, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2002. 40. Orem J et al. studied the feasibility of combining serial lumbar punctures and acetazolamide in managing elevated cerebrospinal fluid pressure in AIDS patients with cryptococcal meningitis in Uganda, published in Tropical Doctor in 2005. 41. Rex JH et al. reported on catastrophic visual loss due to Cryptococcus neoformans meningitis, published in Medicine (Baltimore) in 1993. 42. Antinori S et al. reviewed the role of cryptococcal antigen assays in diagnosing and monitoring cryptococcal meningitis, published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2005. 43. Lu H et al. revisited the significance of cryptococcal antigen testing for therapy monitoring in a tertiary Chinese hospital, published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2005. 44. Dismukes WE et al. compared four weeks versus six weeks of combination amphotericin B and flucytosine therapy for cryptococcal meningitis, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1987. 45. Powderly WG et al. evaluated the measurement of cryptococcal antigen in serum and cerebrospinal fluid for managing AIDS-associated cryptococcal meningitis, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1994. 46. Zuger A et al. described the diagnostic features and treatment outcomes of cryptococcal disease in AIDS patients, published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 1986. 47. Haddow LJ et al. proposed clinical case definitions for cryptococcal immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome in HIV-1-infected individuals, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2010. 48. Shelburne SA et al. examined the role of immune reconstitution in managing cryptococcal meningitis.
